105.0.s.en: (1) The call of the believers to praise

105.0.0.en: 1- O give thanks unto the Lord; call upon his name: make known his deeds among the Gentiles.

105.0.1.en: Talk ye of all his wondrous works. 3- Glory ye in his holy name: let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord.

105.0.2.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm calls the believers in God to give thanks to Him and repeat His great name; that is, to remember His gracious person, so that their faith increases, and then he charges them with the responsibility of making the pagan nations know the greatness of God so that they may believe in Him.

105.0.3.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about the work of the Apostles, the priests and the servants in the New Covenant. And it defines for them a basic task: a- Prayer and praise.

105.0.4.en: b- Preaching to unbelievers so that they may know God and His works with His people.

105.0.5.en: 3- The writer of the Psalm calls the believers to glory in God, and not in material things, or positions, or power, as Peter did with the lame man at the Beautiful Gate, so he healed him in the name of Christ (Acts 3:6). And the glorying is in God, because He is able to do all things, and loves His children and answers them.

105.0.6.en: 4- The inevitable result of praise, preaching and glorying in the Lord is that a person rejoices and enjoys fellowship with God.

105.1.0.en: 4- Seek the Lord, and his strength: seek his face evermore. 5- Remember his marvellous works that he hath done; his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth; 6- O ye seed of Abraham his servant, ye children of Jacob his chosen. 7- He is the Lord our God: his judgments are in all the earth.

105.1.1.en: 1- The people of God in the Old Testament, who are the descendants of Abraham and Jacob, seek the Lord and seek His face, and remember His miraculous works with them. By this praise their faith is confirmed and they rejoice.

105.1.2.en: And seeking the Lord is not only by words, but also by obeying His commandments, and especially when a person feels his sin and weakness, he seeks God and asks for Him with humility, need and faith.

105.1.3.en: 2- The face of the Lord points to the Incarnation of the Lord of glory Jesus Christ, and consequently the seed of Abraham, and the people of God in the New Testament, are the Christians; because the Lord's judgments are in all the earth (v. 7) and not only for the Jews, for the Gentiles believed in Christ in addition to the Jews.

105.1.4.en: I wish, my brother, that in all your needs and afflictions you would seek God first, and lean on Him before you think of people or money, while taking care to do your duty with all your energy; and trust that God hears you and moves the whole universe for your sake, and be at ease because He is your God who loves you.

105.2.s.en: (2) God's promise to Abraham and his seed

105.2.0.en: 8- He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations. 9- Which covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath unto Isaac; 10- And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant: 11- Saying, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance.

105.2.1.en: The lot of your inheritance: in ancient times land was measured by the cord, so what is meant is the land of Canaan, whose measure by the cord was known, which God gave to His people, and He drove out its wicked inhabitants from it and destroyed them.

105.2.2.en: 1- God promised Abraham to give him the land of Canaan, for him and for his seed (Gen 13:14, 15). And He swore to Isaac that He would give him Canaan as an inheritance (Gen 26:3, 4). And likewise to Jacob the son of Isaac He confirmed this promise (Gen 28:13-15), and especially after He changed the name of Jacob to Israel He affirmed the promise (Gen 35:9-15). And although they did not receive these promises in their lifetime, God is true in His promises, and He gave it to their seed.

105.2.3.en: 2- God's promise to the fathers was to a thousand generations (v. 8), and by this He means eternity (v. 10), for these promises of blessing are not meant only for the seed of Abraham in the Old Testament, but rather the seed of Abraham in the New Testament, that is, the Christians, those who do the works of Abraham (Jn 8:39), to whom He will give the Kingdom of Heaven as an eternal inheritance, and not merely the land of Canaan that flows with milk and honey.

105.3.0.en: 12- When they were but a few men in number; yea, very few, and strangers in it. 13- When they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people; 14- He suffered no man to do them wrong: yea, he reproved kings for their sakes; 15- Saying, Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm.

105.3.1.en: 1- The descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were a small number, seventy persons (Ex 1:5); they moved from the land of Canaan and went to Egypt, then returned from it to the land of Canaan, after they had multiplied and become two million, but they were strangers. For the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob lived in tents, and their seed who dwelt in the land of Canaan - after four hundred years - continued to keep the Feast of Tabernacles, which reminds them of the sojourning of the world.

105.3.2.en: 2- God preserved the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and reproved kings for their sake when He reproved Pharaoh for the sake of Abraham, and kept his wife so that Pharaoh did not wrong her (Gen 12:17), and Abimelech king of Gerar for the sake of Isaac (Gen 20:3). And Laban for the sake of Jacob his sister's son, so He did not allow him to harm him (Gen 32, 33). And when He says "Touch not mine anointed" He means the fathers, and although they were not anointed with oil like the priests and the prophets who came from their seed, they were anointed by the Holy Spirit, and received many blessings, like those who were anointed with oil. And God called them prophets although they did not prophesy, but they were like the prophets, that is, anointed by the Holy Spirit (Gen 20:6, 7).

105.3.3.en: If you are weak and have only a little, trust that by the blessing of God you will become many; for God blesses you and keeps you, and reproves the demons who try to harm you.

105.4.s.en: (3) Joseph from prison to the throne

105.4.0.en: 16- Moreover he called for a famine upon the land: he brake the whole staff of bread.

105.4.1.en: The staff of bread: a wooden staff on which bread is kept.

105.4.2.en: God permitted a great famine in Egypt and all the neighboring countries, and God broke everything in which bread is kept, or from which bread could be made, that is, there was no longer any food in the land. And this famine was an opportunity for Joseph the righteous to shine as manager not only of Egypt but of the whole earth, so he fed them, and the descendants of Jacob came to Egypt to sojourn there, and Joseph provided for them.

105.5.0.en: 17- He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant: 18- Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron: 19- Until the time that his word came: the word of the Lord tried him. 20- The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free. 21- He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance:

105.5.1.en: 1- Joseph's brothers rose against him and sold him as a slave, and he came to Egypt to work in the house of Potiphar, and Potiphar's wife rose against him with her lust, but he refused evil, so he was thrown into prison and bound with iron.

105.5.2.en: All this was by God's permission, to prepare a place for the people of the sons of Jacob, and to prepare Joseph spiritually and psychologically, so that he would be strengthened and trust in God through the sufferings and his holding fast to purity. So God tested Joseph and he succeeded greatly, and he always enjoyed fellowship with God.

105.5.3.en: 2- God promised Joseph long before, through his dreams, that he would be a ruler over his brothers, and years passed in which God tested him with many afflictions in the land of Egypt, until the time came in which the word of God was fulfilled, when Pharaoh dreamed his dream and no one interpreted it for him. And although Joseph had interpreted a dream for the king's cupbearer in prison, and asked him to remember him to the king, he forgot him for two years, until the king's cupbearer remembered Joseph when an interpreter was needed for Pharaoh's dream. So the word of God was fulfilled, and Pharaoh summoned him and he interpreted the dream and gave him the solution, so he made him ruler over all Egypt. God cares for His children through afflictions, and fulfills His promises at the right time, and raises them above all they imagine, as He raised Joseph to the throne of Egypt.

105.6.0.en: 22- To bind his princes at his pleasure; and teach his senators wisdom. 23- Israel also came into Egypt; and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.

105.6.1.en: To bind his princes: the rulers of Egypt submit to Joseph.

105.6.2.en: His senators: the elders of Egypt learned from Joseph's wisdom and management.

105.6.3.en: The land of Ham: the land of Egypt.

105.6.4.en: Joseph ruled over all Egypt, and gathered the wheat into storehouses, and all the rulers of Egypt, indeed the whole world, submitted to him. And when the famine came, and all the Egyptians came to buy from him, they even sold themselves as slaves, after Joseph had bought everything that was in Egypt and made it subject to Pharaoh. And Joseph's brothers and his father came to Egypt to live in it, and Joseph hosted them, and they lived. All this arrangement was from God so that His people would not perish from hunger, and He used Joseph to provide for them.

105.6.5.en: God arranges your whole life, so do not be troubled however many afflictions come upon you, for He is able to keep you during them, and to turn every evil into your good, as He did with Joseph, and even to make you grow spiritually, and you feel God with you in everything.

105.7.0.en: 24- And he increased his people greatly; and made them stronger than their enemies.

105.7.1.en: God blessed His people who entered the land of Egypt, who are the descendants of Jacob, and their number was seventy persons (Ex 1:5), and over the years they multiplied abundantly by the grace of God, so that in about four hundred years they became two million persons. This was at first useful to the Egyptians, since they enslaved them and forced them to work in the cities, in addition to shepherding the flocks, but their great increase aroused fear in the hearts of the Egyptians (Ex 1:10), and God permitted the evil that was in the hearts of the Egyptians toward His people to appear, so they tried to humiliate them and force them to work for nothing, hoping that from the toil a great number of them would die, but by the blessing of God their number increased. So they made plans to weaken them, such as killing the male children through the women who deliver the Hebrew women. Then they also schemed against them, as Pharaoh commanded that the male children be thrown into the river Nile, but by the grace of God all these attempts failed, and on the contrary, the more they humiliated them, the more they grew and multiplied (Ex 1:12). For whom God protects and keeps, no one can harm.

105.8.0.en: 26- He sent Moses his servant; and Aaron whom he had chosen.

105.8.1.en: God chose Moses, who according to Pharaoh's orders was supposed to be drowned in the river, but was brought up by God's arrangement in Pharaoh's palace by the princess, Pharaoh's daughter, who drew him out of the river. And when Moses grew up he went to the wilderness, and there God appeared to him in the bush and called him - he and Aaron his brother - to bring His people out of the land of Egypt. And so God delivered Moses from death, and made him a leader to deliver the people and bring them out of the land of Egypt. How wonderful are Your works, O Lord!

105.9.0.en: 27- They shewed his signs among them, and wonders in the land of Ham.

105.9.1.en: God commanded Moses to meet - he and Aaron - the elders of Israel, and to announce to them that God would bring them out of Egypt, and would do signs before them; these were the turning of his rod into a serpent, and the turning of his hand to be leprous, then returning whole, and the turning of water into blood (Ex 4:1-9). So the elders believed and rejoiced. Then Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and asked him to let the children of Israel go out of Egypt, but he did not agree. So God struck Egypt with wonderful signs, which are the ten plagues, and God intended to confirm the faith of His people and to call the Egyptians to faith through these plagues.

105.10.0.en: 28- He sent darkness, and made it dark; and they rebelled not against his word.

105.10.1.en: 1- God struck the Egyptians with ten plagues, and Pharaoh was hard of heart, so he refused to obey God. But in this verse he refers to the ninth plague, and it was severe and shows God's intense wrath; for it was complete darkness over all the land of Egypt, such as Egypt had not seen before. And at the same time there was light in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel lived (Ex 10:21-23). And light is a symbol of the presence of God, while darkness is a symbol of sin and affliction. By this God struck their god Ra, that is, the sun, so that they would feel the weakness of their gods and believe in God.

105.10.2.en: 2- "They rebelled not against his word": this applies to Moses and Aaron in their obedience to God and their confronting Pharaoh. And nature also did not rebel against God. As for the Egyptians, they obeyed God because of the severity of this trial, and they sent out the children of Israel after the next plague. For the ninth plague, in its severity, was a preparation for the most severe of the plagues, the tenth, concerning the killing of the firstborn.

105.11.0.en: 29- He turned their waters into blood, and slew their fish.

105.11.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm returns to the first plague, which was the turning of the river Nile, and all the waters that were in Egypt, into blood. By this He struck one of their great gods, the Nile, so that they would not worship it because of its weakness. And at the same time He caused them a huge problem, for they found no water to drink, so they were forced to dig wells of water to drink (Ex 7:19-25).

105.11.2.en: 2- It was not the turning of the river to a red color but real blood, and the proof of this is that the fish that lived in the Nile died and stank, that is, the Nile and all that was in it lost life, and became a source of distress and disgust.

105.12.0.en: 30- Their land brought forth frogs in abundance, in the chambers of their kings. 31- He spake, and there came divers sorts of flies, and lice in all their coasts.

105.12.2.en: 1- The second plague on Egypt was the frogs, which spread in abundance in all the land, and entered the houses, the palaces and the temples, and defiled everything in Egypt, so they showed the weakness of the priests and the gods.

105.12.3.en: 2- The frogs also entered Pharaoh's palace and the princes of Egypt, and troubled them, and defiled their houses, until they were very distressed. And they gathered the frogs that died and stank, and they corrupted the air of Egypt (Ps 78:45). All this in the hope that they would repent and return to God.

105.12.4.en: 3- The third plague was the gnats, which spread in the land of Egypt, and with their stings troubled the Egyptians severely. And the fourth plague was the flies (resembling the beetle), which spread among the Egyptians with their gloomy appearance and troubled them. All this was in Egypt except the land of Goshen in which the children of Israel lived, which was not exposed to the ten plagues (Ex 8:22, 23).

105.13.0.en: 32- He gave them hail for rain, and flaming fire in their land. 33- He smote their vines also and their fig trees; and brake the trees of their coasts.

105.13.1.en: 1- The seventh plague was the falling of hail, which is sheets of ice that kill whomever they strike. And strangely, it was accompanied by fire from heaven to destroy the Egyptians. So it was a violent plague that killed many of the Egyptians who were outside their houses (Ex 9:18).

105.13.2.en: 2- This plague broke the trees and the plants and burned them, so it ruined and devastated the land of Egypt, in the hope that this affliction would bring the Egyptians back to the mighty God, who surpasses all their gods.

105.14.0.en: 34- He spake, and the locusts came, and caterpillars, and that without number, 35- And did eat up all the herbs in their land, and devoured the fruit of their ground.

105.14.1.en: Caterpillars: small locusts not yet fully grown.

105.14.2.en: The eighth plague was the swarms of locusts that attacked Egypt in huge numbers, in its different stages, whether the young locusts or the large locusts, which ate every green plant in Egypt, so they completed the ruin of the land after the plague of hail and fire. And by this the land of Egypt was utterly destroyed (Ex 10:12-15).

105.15.0.en: 36- He smote also all the firstborn in their land, the chief of all their strength.

105.15.1.en: The tenth and last plague was the most severe of the plagues; for it killed all the firstborn of Egypt, man and beast, even the firstborn of Pharaoh, and it was terrifying as it took place at midnight, so there was crying and weeping in all Egypt. So Pharaoh finally submitted, and let the children of Israel go out of the land of Egypt.

105.16.0.en: 37- He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes. 38- Egypt was glad when they departed: for the fear of them fell upon them.

105.16.1.en: 1- When Pharaoh let the children of Israel go out of Egypt, God gave them strength, so there was no sick or weak person among them. And they asked the Egyptians for silver and gold, and they gave them in abundance, to please them and bring them out of their land, since they were in great terror of them.

105.16.2.en: 2- Despite Egypt's grief over its firstborn, it was glad to be rid of the power of the God of the children of Israel, who had terrified them. And the children of Israel were glad at the power of their God and their liberation from the slavery of Egypt.

105.16.3.en: I wish you would rely on God and trust in Him more than in every power you depend on, whether your understanding, or your position, or your knowledge, or your various abilities, for they are nothing before the power of God. And however great your weakness, you are stronger than all around you because of God's work in you and through you.

105.17.s.en: (5) The wilderness of Sinai and the entry into Canaan

105.17.0.en: 39- He spread a cloud for a covering; and fire to give light in the night.

105.17.2.en: 1- When God brought His people out of Egypt, and their number was about two million persons (six hundred thousand men besides women and children) (Ex 12:37), He shaded them with the cloud so that the sun would not burn them. And at the same time the cloud went before them and they walked behind it. And at night a pillar of fire appeared to them, going before them to guide them in the way and give them light. And so God appears as the leader of His people, and their Father who cares for them and guides them.

105.17.3.en: 2- God always shades His children and guides them, and works by His Holy Spirit in their hearts like fire to burn up their sins and kindle their hearts with His love.

105.18.0.en: 40- The people asked, and he brought quails, and satisfied them with the bread of heaven. 41- He opened the rock, and the waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places like a river.

105.18.1.en: The quail (salwa): a kind of migratory bird resembling the quail (samman).

105.18.2.en: 1- God cared to provide for His people and feed them, so He gave them the bread of heaven every morning, which is the manna, and gave them also the quails, that they might be satisfied with meat and lack nothing. As for water, it came out for them from the rock when Moses struck it with the rod. So the people of God saw that their God is mighty, able to feed them in the barren wilderness with food and drink, however many they were, so that their faith in Him would be confirmed.

105.18.3.en: 2- The coming down of the manna from heaven, and the quails with the wind, lifts the hearts of the people to God who is able to feed them spiritually also. And the wind is a symbol of the Spirit, for the Holy Spirit is the One who gives them life.

105.18.4.en: And the rock is a symbol of Christ, who by His death on the cross gave them the Holy Spirit, who is symbolized by the water of life and the river that flows in the dry wilderness of our hearts.

105.19.0.en: 42- For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham his servant. 43- And he brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness:

105.19.1.en: God promised Abraham to bless him and his seed, and although long years passed, about four hundred years, God does not forget His promises or go back on them, so He remembered it, that is, He fulfilled it at the right time, and brought His people out by the might of His arm, and parted the Red Sea for them, so they crossed over, and Pharaoh and all his army perished because of the hardness of his heart. For after he let the people of the children of Israel go, he came back and felt the loss to Egypt in the departure of two million slaves, so he rose to pursue them to bring them back, and was drowned in the Red Sea. And when the people of God saw the power of their God in saving them from Pharaoh and his drowning, they praised Him and sang under the leadership of Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron, and this is the spiritual satisfaction after they had been satisfied materially.

105.20.0.en: 44- And gave them the lands of the heathen: and they inherited the labour of the people; 45- That they might observe his statutes, and keep his laws. Praise ye the Lord.

105.20.1.en: 1- God punished the pagan peoples who lived in the land of Canaan for their many sins, toward which God had been very long-suffering, so He finally drove them out of the land of Canaan, and settled His people who believe in Him in their place.

105.20.2.en: 2- By the children of Israel's possession of the land of Canaan, the promise of God that He gave to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob was fulfilled. And the fulfillment of this promise helps the people of God to wait for the promise of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, to live with God until they reach the Kingdom of Heaven.

105.20.3.en: 3- The condition for the children of Israel's remaining firm in the land of Canaan was their keeping God's laws and statutes.

105.20.4.en: So because of their faith they remain in the land, just as God, because of the unbelief of the pagans, drove them out of their land.

105.20.5.en: 4- God, who keeps His children, and guides them and provides for them in the wilderness of Sinai, completes His work, and brings them in and settles them in a land flowing with milk and honey, that is, abundant good things, and that is the land of Canaan.

105.20.6.en: As much as you hold fast to God's commandments you receive His power and His blessings, and by your keeping the commandment it keeps you in all your ways until it brings you to eternal bliss.

105.20.7.en: The people's rebellion and God's kindnesses: "Praise ye the Lord. O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

105.20.8.en: "Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord?" (vv. 1, 2) Introduction:

105.20.9.en: 1- Its writer: It is a Psalm without a title, that is, one of the "orphan" Psalms whose writer is not known. But many of the Fathers incline to attribute it to David.

105.20.10.en: 2- When was it written? When the ark was brought back to Jerusalem from the house of Obed-edom the Gittite (1 Chr 16:

105.20.11.en: 34-36), because it glorifies God who abounds in kindness. And there is another opinion that David wrote it when he was a fugitive in Gath, therefore it says "gather us from among the heathen" (v. 47).

105.20.12.en: 3- There is a similarity between this Psalm and the one before it (Ps 105), for the first tells us of God's care for His people, while this Psalm tells us of God's faithfulness to His people despite their disobedience.

105.20.13.en: 4- There is some similarity between this Psalm and (1 Chr 16), in which the bringing back of the ark of the covenant of God is mentioned.

105.20.14.en: 5- There is a similarity between this Psalm and the prayers of Ezra (Ezra 9), Nehemiah (Neh 9), Daniel (Dan 9), and Baruch (Bar 2); in all of these the writer mentions the rebellion and errors of the people of God, and on the other hand God's faithfulness, love and kindness.

105.20.15.en: 6- This Psalm shows the ugliness of our sins before God's kindnesses; therefore we praise Him. The meaning of this is that my falling into sin calls me to repentance, and does not hinder me from prayer and praise.

105.20.16.en: 7- This Psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.

105.20.17.en: 8- This Psalm is among the Psalms that begin and end with Alleluia, and they are eight Psalms, which are, besides this Psalm, Pss 111, 113, 135, 146, 148, 149, 150.
